name: High-dose / intermediate-dose cytarabine (AML postremission consolidation)

source.textbook: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22nd ed. (2025)
source.nccnTemplate: pending - per-disease NCCN Chemotherapy Order Template not yet provided

institution.provenance: textbook-grounded draft; NCCN per-disease template + clinical (StewardMD) + hospital/institutional approval pending

premedications.name: Ocular prophylaxis (corticosteroid eye drops)
premedications.notes: standard supportive-care practice with high-dose cytarabine to reduce keratoconjunctivitis; dose not printed in source, per institutional protocol

supportiveCare: Antiemetics: moderate emetic risk tier per NCCN Antiemesis framework (Appendix D) - cytosine arabinoside >1 g/m2 classified as moderately emetogenic (30-90% risk) in Harrison's, ed. 22, line 83757

G-CSF: consolidation regimens with HiDAC/IDAC are myelosuppressive; per NCCN Appendix C, high-risk regimens warrant prophylactic CSF support - regimen-specific NCCN Growth Factors algorithm entry not yet confirmed, verify before finalizing
Administration sequence: single-agent regimen, no NCCN Appendix F sequencing applicable (only one drug class given)
monitoring: Neurologic exam before each dose of high-dose cytarabine (cerebellar toxicity risk with HiDAC)
Renal function (dose-dependent cerebellar/renal toxicity risk rises with impaired creatinine clearance)

doseModificationRules.text: Review required. Protocol-specific delay/reduce criteria may apply; physician decides.

doseModificationRules.condition: Cerebellar toxicity (ataxia, dysarthria, nystagmus) on exam prior to a dose
doseModificationRules.text: Hold remaining HiDAC doses for the cycle; physician decides on resumption/dose reduction.

drugs.name: Cytarabine
drugs.notes: High-dose (HiDAC) option. Printed verbatim in Harrison's 22nd ed. as 3 g/m2 every 12 h on days 1, 3, and 5 (converted to 3000 mg/m2 here). Source states this longstanding practice may not improve survival over IDAC. Alternative to cytarabine-idac below; physician selects one dosing strategy per patient risk group, not both together.

drugs.name: Cytarabine
drugs.notes: Intermediate-dose (IDAC), ELN-preferred option for favorable/intermediate-risk younger patients, for two to four cycles. Source prints a range of 1-1.5 g/m2 every 12 h on days 1-3 (no single value distinguished as more-printed); this entry uses the 1.5 g/m2 upper bound of the printed range - confirm the intended dose within the 1-1.5 g/m2 range against the institutional order before use. Source notes younger, favorable-risk patients have worse outcomes at doses <1 g/m2. For favorable-risk OLDER patients, source separately prints an attenuated dose of 0.5-1 g/m2 every 12 h on days 1-3 (not encoded as a separate drug entry here; see notes only - dose not selected as a discrete printed value, verify).
